stem.text: The diagram shows the distribution of molecular energies in a sample of gas at a temperature $T_1$. The activation energy for an uncatalysed reaction of this gas, $E_{\text{a(uncat)}}$, is shown.

stem.alt: Graph of proportion of molecules with a given energy against molecular energy E, with a curve peaking at T1 and a dashed line labelled Ea(uncat) to the right of the peak.

stem.text: Which diagram correctly shows the new distribution and new activation energy, $E_{\text{a(cat)}}$, when the temperature is increased to $T_2$, and a catalyst is used that increases the rate of the reaction?

A.alt: Graph with T2 dashed curve peaking at lower energy than T1, with Ea(uncat) and Ea(cat) lines, Ea(cat) to the right of Ea(uncat).

B.alt: Graph with T2 dashed curve peaking at lower energy, with Ea(cat) line to the left of Ea(uncat) line.

C.alt: Graph with T2 dashed curve peaking at higher energy than T1 and a lower peak, with Ea(cat) line to the left of Ea(uncat) line.

D.alt: Graph with T2 dashed curve peaking at higher energy than T1, with Ea(uncat) line to the left of Ea(cat) line.
